Subject: Req: Air-gapped install & operational controls for Redwood Private

Sofia —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement for the Redwood Private (air-gapped) offering we need a compact, actionable set of materials to validate install and ongoing operations. Specifically we need:

- An installation checklist that an on-prem ops engineer can follow end-to-end for a completely offline install (no inbound outbound network).
- How the installer is signed and how GlacierTech verifies the signature prior to install (verification commands/examples).
- SBOM snapshot for the installer and a statement of how SBOMs will be delivered for future updates.
- Offline patching workflow (how patches are delivered, validated, and applied) and expected cadence.
- Evidence of key separation / KMS approach for air-gapped: support for HSM or wrapped key import, and sample config.

Deliverables can be attachments or links. Ideally we get an operational runbook we can review this week.

-James

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

James —

Thanks, and great to meet you (virtually). Attached is a concise package that addresses each bullet: an installation checklist, an SBOM snapshot for the current v2.1 installer, and the signed installer signature. Highlights below: 

- Installer signing: we sign release bundles with an organizational GPG key and provide SHA256 checksums and an accompanying .sig file. Verification steps are in the checklist ("gpg --verify" and checksum verification examples).
- SBOM delivery: we attach a snapshot (SBOM JSON) and we commit to producing an SBOM with every signed release. For customers on Private we can also provide a weekly delta SBOM archive on request (delivered via encrypted removable media/image).
- Offline patching: standard flow is (1) we publish a signed patch bundle, (2) customer downloads via portal to an air-gapped transfer medium, (3) local ops verifies signature + checksum, (4) apply with the bundled CLI which performs a transactional upgrade with rollback. Expected default cadence: security patches as needed (emergency), minor patches monthly, major upgrades scheduled and tested with customer.
- KMS / key separation: Private supports two models: HSM-backed keys via PKCS#11 (customers supply HSM info), or pre-wrapped keys (we provide tooling to wrap/unbundle keys offline). We include sample config snippets in the checklist and notes on rotating keys offline.

Attachments included: airgap-install-checklist.xlsx, sbom-snapshot-20280615.json, signed-installer-v2.1.tar.gz.sig

We also have a longer ops runbook with recovery and upgrade playbooks — sharing a read-only Drive link below. If you want, we can set up a short walkthrough next week and we can demo verification commands against a sample image.

Drive runbook link: https://drive.redwood.company/shared/GlacierTech/airgap-runbook-v1.2

Best,

Sofia — thanks for the package. A couple follow-ups after a quick read: 

1) Installer chain-of-trust: do you provide an intermediate signing cert per-customer (so we can rotate without requiring new root releases), or do we verify solely against Redwood's org key? If the former, what is the provisioning flow for the intermediate cert into the air-gapped environment?

2) During offline upgrades we need a deterministic attestable step for the ops team to confirm that the image was not tampered with after transfer. Can you provide example commands that we can add to our automation (e.g., verify checksum -> verify signature -> verify installer manifest) and sample output?

3) Can you confirm whether the installer performs pre-flight checks for local kernel modules and required kernel parameters? If a kernel change is required, what is the recommended process for scheduling (we are highly change-controlled).

If you can include a single-page runbook excerpt showing the three verification commands and the HSM import example that would be ideal.

-James

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: James Park (GlacierTech) <j.park@glaciertech.com>
Cc: security@glaciertech.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 17 Jun 2028 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Req: Air-gapped install & operational controls for Redwood Private

James —

Appreciate the precision. Attached is a one‑page verification excerpt plus a short HSM import example and expected CLI output. Summary answers: 

1) Signing model: we support both models. By default we sign releases with Redwood org keys. For customers requiring independent rotation we support per-customer intermediate signing certificates; provisioning is done out-of-band via an agreed transfer mechanism (signed CSR exchange) and the intermediate certificate is stored locally in the customer's HSM or as an encrypted wrapped key. We include commands for importing a PEM certificate into common appliances (example for OpenSC / PKCS#11 and Thales).

2) Deterministic verification commands (excerpt):
- sha256sum signed-installer-v2.1.tar.gz
- gpg --verify signed-installer-v2.1.tar.gz.sig signed-installer-v2.1.tar.gz
- redwood-installer verify-manifest --manifest manifest.json --signature manifest.sig

Sample successful output is in the attached excerpt. Our installer also writes an install.log with SHA256 of installed artifacts and signs that log with the local wrapped key for audit ingest.

3) Pre-flight kernel checks: installer performs a pre-flight audit for required kernel params and modules (lists presented during pre-check). If a kernel change is required we recommend scheduling during your standard maintenance window. The installer provides a dry-run flag so you can surface required changes without applying them.

Attachments: airgap-install-checklist.xlsx (updated with CLI snippets), sbom-snapshot-20280615.json, signed-installer-v2.1.tar.gz.sig, verification-excerpt.txt
